title: Faculty Survey Questionnaire
purpose: This survey aims to assess the work environment, management efficiency, and resource adequacy within the Law Discipline. Your feedback is essential for the Self-Assessment Report (SAR) required for BAC Accreditation.
confidentiality: This survey is strictly anonymous. Data will be aggregated for quality assurance purposes only. No individual will be identified in the reporting.
scale: 1 = Strongly Disagree / Very Poor | 2 = Disagree / Poor | 3 = Neutral / Average | 4 = Agree / Good | 5 = Strongly Agree / Excellent

sections.title: Part A: Governance, Workload & Strategy (Standard 1 & 7)
sections.focus: Adherence to Law-specific mandates on workload and planning.

questions.text: Workload: My teaching load per semester does not exceed 12 credits, allowing time for research and counseling.
Class Size: The number of students in my theory classes (max 40) and practical classes (max 20) is appropriate for effective teaching.
Strategic Planning: I am involved in the strategic planning process and aware of the program's vision and mission.
Teacher-Student Ratio: The department maintains a reasonable teacher-student ratio (approx. 1:20).
Autonomy: I have sufficient academic autonomy to design courses and introduce innovative teaching methods.
Curriculum Review: The curriculum is reviewed regularly with input from industry experts and alumni.
Alignment: My Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs) are clearly aligned with the Program Learning Outcomes (PLOs) and Graduate Attributes.
Pedagogy: I frequently use interactive methods (e.g., case studies, mooting, problem-based learning) rather than traditional lecturing.
HOTS: My teaching and assessment methods focus on Higher Order Thinking Skills (analysis, evaluation, creation).
Course Files: I maintain a documented course file (lesson plan, assessment tools, rubrics) for every course I teach.
Feedback: I provide timely feedback to students on their assignments and continuous assessments.
Research Support: The institution provides adequate financial support/grants for research activities.
Publications: I am encouraged and supported to publish research in peer-reviewed journals.
Professional Development: The university sponsors my participation in training, seminars, or conferences (home/abroad).
Incentives: There is a clear policy for incentives/rewards for high-quality research and teaching excellence.
Leave Policy: The study leave policy supports faculty pursuing advanced degrees (PhD/MPhil).
Moot Court: The Moot Court Room is well-equipped (internet, sound system) and available for my classes.
Library: The library has sufficient law books, journals, and e-resources to support my teaching and research.
IT Resources: The IT facilities (internet, computers, software) are adequate for academic purposes.
Office Environment: I have a dedicated workstation and a congenial office environment.

sections.title: Part E: Institutional Integrity & Student Support (Standard 3 & 6)

questions.text: Recruitment: The faculty recruitment and promotion process is transparent, fair, and merit-based.
Code of Conduct: There is a well-defined code of conduct for faculty and staff.
Counseling: I am actively involved in academic guidance and counseling for students.
Performance Evaluation: The performance evaluation system (KPIs) is clear, fair, and communicated effectively.
